mand /recap command.
# Turn Recap for DSH

A persistent DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that writes a short,
model-generated recap under every co
mpleted turn in the Web UI — and regenerates one on demand with `/recap`.
English | 中文
## What it does
- **After a turn the session goes quiet** a card appears at the end of that turn: one to three sente

nces saying what the
turn accomplished and, only when it matters, what is still unfinished. The card

waits out a quiet window (two minutes
by default) and never appears for a turn you kept working pas

t — it is a "where did I leave off" card, not a second
summary of a reply you are still reading. The

text follows the conversation's language.
- **`/recap`** produces the same card for the latest turn

on demand, immediately — useful when a turn never got its quiet
window, when you scrolled past it,

or when you want a fresh read of where things stand.
- Turns that carry nothing to summarize (interr

upted or failed turns, empty turns) produce no card, and subagent
sessions are skipped by default.
-
When the turn leaves exactly one real next action — an unanswered question, an agreed next step, or

a remedy for a
blocker — the card adds a single **Next step** line under the summary. Turns that fi
nished cleanly get no such line.
The card uses the host's theme tokens, so it follows light/dark and the active locale (English and S

implified Chinese
dictionaries ship with the bundle).
## Requirements
- **DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2`** — the runtime this plugin was built and verified against. `package.json` de

clares that floor as
`engines.dsh`, and the launcher enforces it twice: when the bundle is installed

, and again when a profile holding it
starts. An older runtime refuses the operation with `incompati

ble-version` and names the unmet range.
- Check which runtime a profile will use with `dsh --version

`.
- The floor is the API set this plugin binds, not a guess: `agent/turn-stopping`, session project

ions with a
client-visible `wire` view, the `commands` registry (including `command/done` result tex

t), `llm.prepareCall()`
streaming, and on the Client side the `conversation.chat.turnTail` and `conv

ersation.chat.commandview` slots plus
`remote.session.projections`. A nearby version that provides a

ll of them will almost certainly work, but only the
declared floor is the combination tested here.
No `peerDependencies` are declared on purpose: this bundle imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` module — it o

nly resolves Cordis
services at runtime — so a peer range would describe a dependency that does not

solves Cordis
services at runtime — so a peer range would describe a dependency that does not exist.
If you must run it on an older runtime, the launcher's escape hatch is an exact-version exemption, n
un it on an older runtime, the launcher's escape hatch is an exact-version exemption, never a range:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The same grant is available in Plugin Manager. It authorizes in-process code against a runtime it wa

s never verified
with — crashes and data loss are the documented risk — and it applies to one exact

plugin version on one exact runtime
version.
## Install
This package is a DSH bundle: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and a `dsh.client` half, so it installs

into a profile with
the launcher's own plugin command. Nothing is published to npm.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory and selects the bundle when the install f

inishes. With HMR
enabled in the profile's YAML the composition reloads immediately; otherwise the p

rofile picks it up on the next start.
Install into a named profile by passing it through:

Or ask a DSH session to install the bundle from that directory with the profile's plugin manager.
Reinstalling or toggling the plugin needs no Harness restart: disable and re-enable the row and the

Host module is
imported again.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
1. **`agent/turn-stopping`** is the serial event the agent loop dispatches just before it commits `t

urn/end`. The plugin
digests the turn from the session log — the user request, the newest tool calls

(with failures marked), and the
turn's *final* assistant reply — and asks the model that served the

turn for a short recap.
2. The following **`turn/end`** commit folds the text into the client-visib

le **`recap` session projection**, so the
card and the finished turn arrive in the same frame.
3. Th
e Client half registers into the **`conversation.chat.turnTail`** slot and reads the projection with
`useProjection("recap")`. Each entry carries a `revealAt` deadline: the card is held back until tha

t instant passes
**and** no newer turn has started, so the quiet window costs nothing and the card n
ever interrupts active work.
**What the model is asked for.** One plain-text prompt: one to three sentences in the conversation's

language, precise
about how far the work actually got (`proposed`, `queued`, `implemented`, `tested

`, `published`, and `installed` are
different states), keeping unresolved caveats such as "not insta

lled yet", and treating the latest user message as
scope rather than proof that the work is done. A

real next action — and only a real one — rides in on a final `Next:`
line, which the Host parses int
o its own field so the card can label and style it.
**Why a projection instead of a session event?** A plugin may not append new event types: a log carr

ying a type the
build does not know cannot be reopened, and `appendPluginRecord()` is reserved for f

irst-party experimental packages.
The session projection is the supported carrier for session-derive

rimental packages.
The session projection is the supported carrier for session-derived client state.
**Why is the recap produced before `turn/end`?** Projection state is folded synchronously from commi

tted events and its
Value is only re-read when a committed event changes that state. Producing the t

ext while the turn boundary is still
open is what lets the commitment bake it into state — the delay

ed *appearance* is a client-side rule over the stored
`revealAt`, not a delayed request.
